concepts.def: Back of eye that detects light
Carries signal from eye to brain
Snail-shape part that turns vibration to signal

walkthroughs.body_html:
Light enters through the pupil and hits the retina at the back of the eye.

The retina turns light into electrical signals. The optic nerve sends them to the brain. 👁️

Sound waves wobble the air, which wobbles your eardrum.

Tiny bones pass the vibration to the cochlea — a snail-shape full of fluid.

Hair cells inside turn it into nerve signals for the brain. 👂

Sight and hearing send raw data — the brain decides what it means.

That's why optical illusions and 'did I just hear my name?' moments are so common.

You don't see with eyes — you see with brain. 🧠
